title: Why you check your phone for no reason

lines.text: You pick up your phone. Check it. Put it down.
Ten seconds later, you pick it up again.
Nothing changed. So why do you keep doing it?
In the 1950s, psychologist B. F. Skinner trained pigeons to peck a button for food.
Pigeons that got food every single time pecked calmly.
But pigeons that got food at random, only sometimes, pecked like crazy, and kept going long after the food stopped.
Unpredictable rewards are the hardest to quit.
Sometimes there's a message. Sometimes a like. Most of the time, nothing.
Your brain can't predict which one you'll get, so it keeps pulling the lever.
Your phone is a slot machine in your pocket.
Want to break the loop? Make the lever harder to pull.
Turn off notifications you don't need. Charge your phone in another room. Try grayscale mode, so the screen looks boring.
Be honest. Did you check your phone while watching this?
